sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Smertius is a god of the continental Celts. His other names are Smertrios and Smertrio. He is a lesser and more hidden deity. His name carries the root smer, which also stands in the name of the goddess Rosmerta. The root holds the sense of protecting. One carved figure, taken to be Smertrius, shows a strong man with a beard and the body of a snake below the waist. The figure may show the wrath and the watch of the god together. The word Rosmerta pairs his power with that of the goddess who bears the same root. The two names share the promise of shielding the people who gave them worship, and the record of the carver keeps that old belief.
